real_estate.homebuilder: A new executive order directs FHFA to pilot canceling mortgage insurance once a home's current value shows enough equity, and to cut refinance title costs.
real_estate.commentary:
This week's housing news is about fees, not rates. An executive order signed Oct. 22 directs the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which oversees Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, to set up a pilot that cancels a borrower's mortgage insurance once the home's current market value shows enough equity. It also expands the agency's alternative to lender's title insurance on refinances, and tells USDA and VA to cut rates on the home loans they make directly. (Market Briefs called it canceling insurance on certain new loans; the order ties it to equity.)

Here is why the first piece matters at our prices. A buyer putting 10% down on our five city median of $1,079,000 borrows $971,100, a high balance conforming loan here, and reaches 20% equity once the home is worth about $1,213,900, a 12.5% rise before any principal is paid down. Today, getting that insurance dropped on a higher value usually means asking the servicer and paying for an appraisal; the order asks FHFA to cut those costs. Nothing changes until FHFA writes the rules.

Today's chart is a different kind of neighbor problem. S&P Global Ratings counts 146 U.S. data center projects delayed or canceled, about three quarters of them tied to local pushback, and local governments in 40 states have imposed bans. The top complaints are energy costs, water, air pollution and noise, which will sound familiar to anyone who has sat through a planning commission meeting.

Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average stands at 7.33% and the 15-year at 6.98% from Friday, with Monday's reading due later today, and the Fed meets Tuesday and Wednesday. Locally, inventory barely moved: the board wide table slipped to 2,623 from 2,631, with 140 coming soon and 192 brand new. The five city ledger held at 686, as Hayward rose to 201 from 198, Newark slipped to 90 from 91 and Union City to 65 from 67, while Fremont (227) and Milpitas (103) held.

What this means for you: if you are buying with less than 20% down, ask your lender how the mortgage insurance comes off, because under the pilot your home's value, not just your payments, could get you there. If you own and are weighing a refinance, ask whether the title waiver could apply to your loan. If you are selling, today's buyer is still pricing a 7.33% payment, so price for that from day one.

• Board wide: 2,623 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 140 coming soon and 192 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 686 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 615 are on the market and 71 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 227 live, 180 active, 30 coming soon and 17 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,325,000 at $798 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 35 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 201, Milpitas 103, Newark 90, Union City 65.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $665 a square foot. 289 homes are priced under a million, and 179 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

economy.commentary:
Today's chart is Germany, with a substitution. Market Briefs charted October's flash PMI surveys from S&P Global and HCOB: the composite slipped to 52.8 from 53.8, below the 53.3 forecast, as services fell to 51.7 while manufacturing rose to 54.2. S&P Global does not allow its PMI data to be copied or redistributed without permission, so we drew the story from Eurostat's official numbers instead.

Those show Germany's factories growing again: manufacturing output rose 0.9% from a year earlier in the second quarter, the first gain since late 2022, after 13 straight quarters of decline. The October surveys suggest factories are still doing the lifting while services cool.

At home, the University of Michigan's final October sentiment index read 48.0, its lowest since May, and year ahead inflation expectations ticked up to 4.7% from 4.6%. One correction: Market Briefs printed the 10-Year at 4.96% and gold up 0.01%; Treasury's Friday close was 5.00%, and gold settled down 1.29%.

feature_image.alt: Bar chart of German manufacturing output, percent change from a year earlier, by quarter from 2022 Q1 to 2026 Q2, with a line for the whole economy. Manufacturing fell for 13 straight quarters from 2023 Q1 (down 0.2%) through 2026 Q1 (down 0.5%), with the deepest drop, 4.8%, in 2023 Q4, then rose 0.9% in 2026 Q2, its first gain since late 2022. The whole economy grew 1.1% in 2026 Q2.
feature_image.caption: Germany's manufacturing output rose 0.9% from a year earlier in the second quarter, its first gain since late 2022.
feature_image.source: Source: Eurostat quarterly national accounts, gross value added in chain linked volumes, updated Oct. 22, 2026 (provisional).
